question.worked_solution:
First, note that $x=0$ cannot be a solution. This is because if $x=0,$ then the rational term would be $\frac{7}{0},$ which is undefined because it has a zero denominator.

To solve the equation, we first multiply both sides by the denominator $x$ to get rid of the fraction:

$$
\begin{aligned}14 & =\frac{7}{x} \\ x\cdot 14 & =x\cdot \frac{7}{x} \\ x\cdot 14 & =\cancel{x}\cdot \frac{7}{\cancel{x}} \\ 14x & =7\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we apply the multiplication principle:

$$
\begin{aligned}14x & =7 \\ \frac{14x}{14} & =\frac{7}{14} \\ x & =\frac{1}{2}\end{aligned}
$$

Since  $x=\frac{1}{2}$ is different from $x=0$, we can accept it as a solution.  Thus, the solution is $x=\frac{1}{2}.$
